subject.title: Discord: make native command visibility follow account/channel routing

question: Which Discord command-visibility policy should OpenClaw support for multi-account setups where several Discord apps expose the same native commands?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the gap, but permission syncing, guild-scoped deployment, namespacing, explicit reconcile commands, and documentation-only support have different Discord API, upgrade, propagation, and operator-control tradeoffs.

options.title: Derive Visibility From Routing
options.body: Use existing Discord account/guild/channel routing as the desired command-visibility source after validating Discord permission semantics and propagation behavior.

options.title: Add Explicit Operator Controls
options.body: Add a CLI or config-controlled reconciliation path so operators choose which accounts expose generic commands and when OpenClaw rewrites Discord permissions.

options.title: Document Manual Discord Setup
options.body: Keep OpenClaw execution auth as-is and document manual Discord application command permission setup as the supported multi-account visibility workflow.

recommendation.title: Derive Visibility From Routing
recommendation.body: Use existing Discord account/guild/channel routing as the desired command-visibility source after validating Discord permission semantics and propagation behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the best available routing candidate from current blame on the Discord deploy/docs surface and recent related Discord command history.
